name: Possible Fungal Leaf Spot / Leaf Blight
description: Fungal disease is likely when leaf spots spread during wet or humid conditions.
base_recommendation: Remove heavily infected leaves, avoid overhead watering, improve air circulation, and apply a suitable labelled fungicide if symptoms continue.
consult_expert_when: If the disease spreads quickly, affects many plants, or the crop is commercially valuable, consult an agricultural officer or plant pathologist.

name: Possible Powdery Mildew
description: Powdery mildew is likely when white or grey powdery growth appears on leaves, especially with poor airflow.
base_recommendation: Prune crowded leaves, improve spacing and airflow, avoid wetting leaves, and use an appropriate fungicide when necessary.
consult_expert_when: Consult an expert if powdery growth keeps returning or spreads to young plants.

name: Possible Bacterial Blight
description: Bacterial blight is possible when water-soaked spots or yellow halos appear after wet weather.
base_recommendation: Remove infected plant parts, avoid overhead watering, keep tools clean, and avoid working with plants when foliage is wet.
consult_expert_when: Seek expert confirmation if many leaves show water-soaked lesions or yellow halos.

name: Possible Root Rot / Water Stress
description: Root rot or water stress is possible when plants wilt while soil is too wet or poorly drained.
base_recommendation: Improve drainage, reduce watering frequency, remove severely affected plants, and avoid reusing infected soil without treatment.
consult_expert_when: Consult an expert if roots are dark/soft or the plant collapses suddenly.

name: Possible Nutrient Deficiency
description: Nutrient deficiency is likely when yellowing, pale veins, and slow growth occur without strong disease signs.
base_recommendation: Apply balanced fertilizer according to crop needs, check soil pH, improve organic matter, and monitor new growth after treatment.
consult_expert_when: Seek soil testing or expert advice if yellowing continues after proper fertilization.

name: Possible Pest Infestation
description: Pest infestation is likely when insects, bite holes, sticky residue, eggs, or curling are present.
base_recommendation: Inspect leaf undersides, remove affected leaves, use physical control where possible, and apply suitable pest control based on the identified pest.
consult_expert_when: Consult an expert if pests spread rapidly or if you are unsure which pest control is safe for the crop.

name: Possible Viral Mosaic Disease
description: Viral mosaic disease is possible when mottled leaf patterns, curling, and stunted growth occur, often with pest vectors.
base_recommendation: Remove severely infected plants, control insect vectors, avoid taking cuttings from infected plants, and sanitize tools.
consult_expert_when: Get expert confirmation because viral diseases can be confused with nutrient problems.

name: Possible Drought / Heat Stress
description: Heat or drought stress is possible when wilting happens with dry soil and hot weather, without strong pest or spot symptoms.
base_recommendation: Water deeply at appropriate times, mulch around the plant, provide temporary shade for sensitive crops, and monitor recovery.
consult_expert_when: Seek advice if plants do not recover after proper watering or if root damage is suspected.
